# Beequation

> Beequation is a mental maths puzzle game by Trett Labs Limited (UK). Each honeycomb of numbers hides exactly one number that two others add up to (or multiply to); the player finds and taps it. There are two apps: Beequation Kids (ages 5 to 12) and Beequation (teens and adults), plus a free browser version. No ads, no tracking, no personal data collected; free to try, with a monthly or yearly subscription (7-day free trial) or a one-off Lifetime purchase to unlock every level.

- [Play free online](https://beequation.com/play.html): the browser game, with both the kids and adult versions
- [How to play](https://beequation.com/how-to-play.html): rules, worked examples and tips
- [Free puzzles for teachers](https://beequation.com/teachers.html): printable pack for number bonds to 20 and the 2 to 6 times tables
- [Number bonds to 20: a guide for parents and teachers](https://beequation.com/learn/number-bonds-to-20.html): What number bonds to 10 and 20 are, when children learn them, how to practise them at home or in class, and free honeycomb puzzles that make it fun.
- [Fun ways to practise times tables](https://beequation.com/learn/times-tables-practice.html): Which times tables children learn in each year, what the Year 4 multiplication tables check involves, and quick, fun ways to practise, including free puzzles.
- [Mental maths strategies that really work](https://beequation.com/learn/mental-maths-strategies.html): Eight mental maths strategies for adding, subtracting and multiplying in your head, from bridging through 10 to doubling and halving, with worked examples.
- [A daily maths puzzle for adults](https://beequation.com/learn/daily-maths-puzzle-for-adults.html): Why a short daily number puzzle is a satisfying way to keep your mental arithmetic sharp, and how Beequation's Daily Pro, blitz and expert levels work.
- [Support](https://beequation.com/support.html): purchases, players, refunds and resetting progress
- [Privacy policy](https://beequation.com/privacy.html): the apps collect no personal data
- [About](https://beequation.com/about.html): who makes Beequation

## Learn

Free primary maths guides and worksheets for parents and teachers (Reception to Year 6, National Curriculum in England).

- [Learn maths with Indie](https://beequation.com/learn/): Free primary maths help from Reception to Year 6: topic guides, year-by-year curriculum guides, printable worksheets with answers, and advice for parents and teachers.
- [Maths glossary](https://beequation.com/learn/glossary/): Primary maths words explained in plain English, from acute angle to zero. Each has a worked example and the school year children usually meet it, Reception to Year 6.
- [Maths in everyday life: 38 quick activities](https://beequation.com/learn/parents/everyday-maths.html): Thirty-eight quick ways to practise maths in everyday life with children aged 4 to 11, using cooking, shopping, travel, games, sport, time and money, sorted by age.
- [How to help your child with maths at home](https://beequation.com/learn/parents/helping-at-home.html): Practical ways to help with primary maths at home: little and often, good questions, praising effort, homework help, and what to do when you don't know the method your child uses.
- [How maths is taught in primary schools now](https://beequation.com/learn/parents/how-maths-is-taught.html): Ten frames, part-whole models, number lines, column methods with exchanging, the grid method, bus stop division, chunking and bar models: what they are, when they're taught and why.
- [Maths help for parents](https://beequation.com/learn/parents/): Friendly guides for parents and carers: helping with maths at home, how maths is taught in primary schools now, SATs and the times tables check, maths anxiety and everyday maths activities.
- [Helping a child who says "I'm bad at maths"](https://beequation.com/learn/parents/maths-anxiety.html): What to do when your child says they're bad at maths: the signs of maths anxiety, the words that help ("not yet"), managing your own feelings about maths, low-stakes games, and when to talk to the teacher.
- [Primary school maths tests explained](https://beequation.com/learn/parents/maths-tests-explained.html): Every maths assessment your child meets in primary school in England, from the Reception Baseline Assessment to Year 6 SATs: when they happen, what they involve, what the scores mean and how to help without stress.
- [Differentiation in maths](https://beequation.com/learn/teachers/differentiation-in-maths.html): Practical differentiation for primary maths: keeping the class together, manipulatives, low threshold high ceiling tasks, scaffolds, challenge cards and puzzles for early finishers, with worked examples.
- [Maths resources for teachers](https://beequation.com/learn/teachers/): Free primary maths resources for teachers, Reception to Year 6: quick maths starters, classroom games, reasoning and problem-solving activities, differentiation ideas, printable puzzles and worksheets.
- [Maths games for the classroom](https://beequation.com/learn/teachers/maths-games-for-the-classroom.html): 15 low-prep maths games for primary classrooms, KS1 and KS2: whole-class, pairs and small-group games with the rules, what each one practises and how to adapt it, including honeycomb puzzles on the board.
- [25 quick maths starters](https://beequation.com/learn/teachers/maths-starters.html): 25 quick maths starters for primary classes, grouped for KS1, lower KS2 and upper KS2. Each takes 5 to 10 minutes, needs little or no preparation and comes with a worked example.
- [Reasoning and problem solving](https://beequation.com/learn/teachers/reasoning-and-problem-solving.html): How to build mathematical reasoning and problem solving in primary maths: question stems, convince me, true or false, spot the mistake, open-ended problems, bar models and sentence stems, with examples from Reception to Year 6.
- [Addition and subtraction](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/addition-and-subtraction.html): How children learn addition and subtraction from Reception to Year 6: number bonds, mental methods, number lines and the column method with exchanging, with pictures, common mistakes, games and free worksheets.
- [Algebra and ratio](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/algebra-and-ratio.html): How children learn early algebra and ratio from Reception to Year 6: missing-number problems, patterns and sequences, letters for unknowns, simple formulas, ratio, scale factors and scaling recipes, with examples, games and free worksheets.
- [Counting and place value](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/counting-and-place-value.html): How children learn counting and place value from Reception to Year 6: ones, tens, hundreds and thousands up to millions, comparing, rounding, negative numbers and Roman numerals, with pictures, games and free worksheets.
- [Data and graphs](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/data-and-graphs.html): How children learn about data from Year 2 to Year 6: pictograms, tally charts, bar charts, tables, line graphs, pie charts and the mean, with examples, common mistakes, games and free worksheets.
- [Decimals and percentages](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/decimals-and-percentages.html): How children learn decimals and percentages from Year 3 to Year 6: tenths, hundredths and thousandths, decimal place value, rounding, percentages of amounts and fraction, decimal and percentage equivalents, with pictures, games and free worksheets.
- [Fractions](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/fractions.html): How children learn fractions from Year 1 to Year 6: halves and quarters, equivalent fractions, adding and simplifying, with pictures, common mistakes, games and free worksheets.
- [Maths topics](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/): Twelve free guides to primary maths topics, from counting and place value to algebra and ratio. Each one explains what children learn in each year, with pictures, common mistakes, games and free worksheets.
- [Measurement](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/measurement.html): How children learn measurement from Reception to Year 6: length, mass, capacity and temperature, reading scales, converting metric units, perimeter, area and volume, with pictures, common mistakes, games and free worksheets.
- [Mental maths](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/mental-maths.html): Why mental maths matters, the strategies children learn from Reception to Year 6, how mental and written methods fit together, and the number facts to aim to know by heart, with games and free worksheets.
- [Money](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/money.html): How children learn about money from Year 1 to Year 6: UK coins and notes, counting coins, pounds and pence, making amounts, giving change and shopping problems, with pictures, common mistakes, games and free worksheets.
- [Multiplication and division](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/multiplication-and-division.html): How children learn multiplication and division from Reception to Year 6: arrays, times tables and the Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check, factors and primes, short and long multiplication and division, with pictures, games and free worksheets.
- [Shape and geometry](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/shape-and-geometry.html): How children learn shape and geometry from Reception to Year 6: 2D and 3D shapes, faces, edges and vertices, symmetry, angles, protractors, coordinates, translation and reflection, with pictures, common mistakes, games and free worksheets.
- [Telling the time](https://beequation.com/learn/topics/telling-the-time.html): How children learn to tell the time from Year 1 to Year 6: o'clock and half past, quarter past and quarter to, am and pm, the 24-hour clock and working out how long things take, with pictures, games and free worksheets.
- [Free maths worksheets](https://beequation.com/learn/worksheets/): Free printable primary maths worksheets with answer sheets: number bonds, times tables, column methods, fractions, time, money, shapes, graphs and more, sorted by topic and year group.
- [Maths by year group](https://beequation.com/learn/years/): What children learn in primary maths in each school year, from Reception (age 4 to 5) to Year 6 (age 10 to 11), with ages, US grade equivalents, the key tests and free worksheets.
- [Reception maths: what your child learns (age 4 to 5)](https://beequation.com/learn/years/reception.html): What children learn in maths in Reception (age 4 to 5): the EYFS Early Learning Goals for number, counting, subitising, number bonds to 5 and 10, doubling and sharing, with ideas to help at home.
- [Year 1 maths: what your child learns (age 5 to 6)](https://beequation.com/learn/years/year-1.html): What children learn in Year 1 maths (age 5 to 6) under the National Curriculum: counting to 100, number bonds to 20, halves and quarters, coins, o'clock and half past, and shapes, with tips and worksheets.
- [Year 2 maths: what your child learns (age 6 to 7)](https://beequation.com/learn/years/year-2.html): What children learn in Year 2 maths (age 6 to 7): tens and ones, adding and subtracting to 100, the 2, 5 and 10 times tables, fractions, money and change, time to 5 minutes, and Key Stage 1 SATs.
- [Year 3 maths: what your child learns (age 7 to 8)](https://beequation.com/learn/years/year-3.html): What children learn in Year 3 maths (age 7 to 8): numbers to 1,000, column addition and subtraction, the 3, 4 and 8 times tables, tenths and fractions, perimeter, the 24-hour clock and right angles.
- [Year 4 maths: what your child learns (age 8 to 9)](https://beequation.com/learn/years/year-4.html): What children learn in Year 4 maths (age 8 to 9): all times tables to 12 × 12 and the Multiplication Tables Check, four-digit numbers, negative numbers, decimals, area, coordinates and symmetry.
- [Year 5 maths: what your child learns (age 9 to 10)](https://beequation.com/learn/years/year-5.html): What children learn in Year 5 maths (age 9 to 10): numbers to a million, long multiplication, short division, prime, square and cube numbers, mixed numbers, decimals, percentages and angles in degrees.
- [Year 6 maths: what your child learns (age 10 to 11)](https://beequation.com/learn/years/year-6.html): What children learn in Year 6 maths (age 10 to 11): long division, fractions, decimals and percentages, ratio, algebra, area and volume, pie charts and the mean, plus what to expect from the Key Stage 2 SATs.
